definition: BrownBoost is a boosting algorithm that may be robust to noisy datasets.
details: BrownBoost is an adaptive version of the boost by majority algorithm. As is the case for all boosting algorithms, BrownBoost is used in conjunction with other machine learning methods. BrownBoost was introduced by Yoav Freund in 2001.

explainer.lead: BrownBoost is a boosting algorithm designed to work alongside other machine learning methods. It adapts the boost-by-majority approach and may remain robust when a training dataset contains noise.

tiers.eli5: It's a team of weak guessers whose voting is adjusted so a few bad or noisy members don't ruin the final answer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pair it with other machine learning methods as the base learner, and a pitfall is that it adds tuning complexity over simpler boosting.
tiers.paperLevel: An adaptive version of the boost by majority algorithm introduced by Yoav Freund in 2001, used in conjunction with other machine learning methods; it may be robust to noisy datasets.

explainer.example: Suppose a classifier is trained on 100 labelled examples, 10 of which have incorrect labels. BrownBoost can be used with that classifier’s learning method to produce a boosted predictor, potentially reducing the disruption caused by the noisy labels.
explainer.goal: Build a boosted predictor using other machine learning methods, with possible robustness to noise in the training data.
steps: Apply the accompanying machine learning method.

diagram.caption: BrownBoost works with another learning method to turn possibly noisy training data into a boosted predictor.
